facts.claim: Across a survey of more than 1,000 products, a fifth of freemium products convert below 2.5% and the largest group, a third, sits between 2.5% and 5%
facts.source_title: What is a good free-to-paid conversion rate?
facts.excerpt: A fifth (20%) of products see a conversion rate below 2.5%. About a third see between 2.5% and 5% — the biggest bucket.

facts.claim: Free-trial products convert on a different distribution entirely: only 7% fall below 2.5%, and the most common band is 7.5% to 10%
facts.source_title: What is a good free-to-paid conversion rate?
facts.excerpt: Only 7% of free-trial products see conversion below 2.5%; about a quarter see between 7.5% and 10%, the most common bucket.

facts.claim: AI apps convert free to paid at 1% to 3%, against 5% to 8% for mature subscription mobile apps
facts.source_title: Subscription vs ads for AI apps: which model wins in 2026
facts.excerpt: For AI apps, free-to-paid conversion tends toward 1-3% rather than the 5-8% seen in mature subscription mobile apps.

facts.claim: Across 464 companies the median onboarding tour completion is 29%, with the middle half between 15% and 55%
facts.source_title: Onboarding metrics that predict revenue activation
facts.excerpt: Data from 464 companies shows median tour completion is 29% per company, with the middle half running 15% to 55%.

facts.claim: Onboarding checklists of three to five steps complete at 67%, against 18% for checklists of ten steps or more
facts.source_title: Onboarding metrics that predict revenue activation
facts.excerpt: 3-5 step onboarding checklists complete at 67% vs 18% for 10+ step checklists.

facts.claim: Across 547 companies the median time to value is one day, twelve hours and twenty-three minutes
facts.excerpt: Userpilot's benchmark across 547 SaaS companies places the median time to value at 1 day, 12 hours and 23 minutes.

facts.claim: The top 10% of apps capture 95% of all subscription revenue
facts.source_title: The app middle class is dying, and RevenueCat's data shows how fast
facts.excerpt: The top 10% of apps capture 95% of all subscription revenue.

contradictions: Freemium conversion benchmarks are quoted both as a distribution and as a single ceiling: lennysnewsletter.com reports a fifth of products below 2.5% with the largest group between 2.5% and 5%, while amplitude.com states a benchmark of under 10%. The first describes where products sit and the second where the ceiling is, so they are answers to different questions. Both appear on this page.
